chunks: Al-Saffar narrated from Muhammad ibn 'Isa ibn 'Ubayd from Yunus ibn 'Abd al-Rahman from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) who said:

I said, 'May I be your ransom, what do you say regarding hunting birds in their burrows and wild animals in their habitats at night, for people dislike that?' He said, 'There is no harm in that.' The approach in these narrations is to interpret them as permitting and removing prohibition, and the first two narrations are interpreted as indicating a type of dislike (karahah) short of prohibition (hazr).
ai.seo_question: Is hunting at night considered prohibited or merely disliked in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) establishes the permissibility (jawaz) of hunting birds in their nests and wild animals in their habitats at night, resolving the apparent contradiction with other narrations by distinguishing between strict prohibition (hazr) and recommended dislike (karahat al-nadb). This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of reconciling seemingly conflicting reports by assigning different levels of legal weight, ensuring that general public dislike does not elevate a practice to the status of impermissibility.
